title: Launch strategy railmap and scope-anchor playbook — API/Console/Runtime
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Produce a lightweight, operational playbook that binds milestone gating, scope-anchor rules, and cut criteria across API, Console, and Runtime teams to streamline the Q2 release train. This ticket defines: the milestone calendar; scope-anchor (what cannot change post-freeze); explicit cut gates per lane; release-notes ownership and templating; cross-team communications cadence; rollback thresholds and monitoring signals; and the post-launch observability checklist.

Why this is different: existing release playbooks are launch-heavy checklists. This artefact is a working railmap intended to be updated during triage and will be the single source of truth for decisions that change the release's scope. It prioritizes decision inertia reduction — i.e., clear anchors and fast delegation paths when an exception is needed.

Outcomes expected:
- Shared milestone calendar with owners and primary/secondary contacts.
- Scope-anchor table that lists features and their freeze dates and allowed exceptions.
- Cut criteria per component (API, Console, Runtime) with quantifiable SLO/bug thresholds.
- A release-notes coordination plan (templates + publish schedule + owners).
- Post-launch metrics dashboard requirements and on-call runbook snippets.

Where to find artifacts: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/Q2-2025-Release-Train (draft) | Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/release-q2-2025/railmap | GitHub board: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-planning/boards/q2-2025

rollout_plan: Day -10 to -7: Final compatibility smoke tests between API and Console; record baseline metrics.
Day -6 to -4: Lock release-notes and user-facing change log; prepare customer comms draft.
Day -3 to -1: Run controlled canary in two regions (us-west, eu-west) with 5% traffic each.
Day 0: Increase to 25% and validate KPIs for 2h, then 50% if signal clean; follow canary checklist.
Day +1 to +7: Monitor regressions and user feedback; keep rollback criteria and hotfix slots reserved.
cut_criteria: API: Any regression causing > 0.5% increase in 99th latency vs baseline in canary for 30m => hold rollout
Console: Any UI error rate > 1% on primary flows (login, model selection, deploy) during canary => rollback
Runtime: If tail memory usage increases > 15% or token throughput drops > 10% on dedicated tests => pause
Cross-component: Any data confidentiality risk flagged by Security or a P0 bug => immediate cut and incident bridge
Documentation: Release notes must be completed and reviewed by Docs + PM before global rollout
monitoring_signals: 99th p95/p99 latency by model and endpoint (API)
Token throughput and KV cache hit ratio (Runtime)
Customer-facing errors surfaced via Sentry and Support tickets
Cost anomaly alerts (unexpected per-token cost spikes)
risk_mitigations: If canary fails, automatic fallback to previous model variant (runtime) for 30m while triage runs
Reserve hotfix window: two 2-hour slots per weekday for first week post-launch
Hold-back: Keep a 10% capacity cushion in Dedicated pools for rollback contingencies
Run a final cross-team runbook rehearsal 72 hours before freeze
Pre-authorize emergency scope reduction: a checklist of non-customer-facing features that can be removed without comms
